transcript: Last night I saw Here We Are at The Shed, the musical Stephen Sondheim was working on when he died. And, oh, boy. I didn't really know anything about this going in, and I would recommend experiencing it that way. All you really need to know is that it's good, it's complex, it's incredibly acted by stacked cast, and the space is pretty intimate. I have a hard time believing there are a lot of bad seats. I also thought The Shed was kind of a perfect venue for this show because it's so removed from the rest of Manhattan, and Hudson Yards in general has this very, like, sterile vibe to me, which makes producing Here We Are in that space somewhat ironic due to the themes of the show. The show itself is very difficult to describe in terms of plot. It's definitely more of a concept show, and the concepts are incredibly relevant and cleverly explored. The music is very Sondheim, which is exciting, but the book also really shines. It's funny, it's original and weird. Overall, the show is one of the strangest things I've ever seen on stage, and I love that about it. It's definitely not perfect, but to even have this last Sondheim piece produced at such a high caliber, such a gift. So for that reason, I think it's a must see. Here We Are is currently running at The Shed through mid January next year, so if you wanna see it, don't wait. With that, another program for my collection.
